keyTakeaways: Sort Diwali messages by closeness: about 5 people get a personal memory, the outer circle of about 150 gets short thanks (Dunbar 2016 layers).
Keep most messages under 40 words; 48.3% of SubhSandesh pages are opened on a phone.
Cousins tolerate silence better than friends: 70.3% of inner-layer relatives stayed close over 18 months, against 48.6% of friends (Roberts & Dunbar 2015).
To restart contact, send one memory and one question on Friday 29 October 2027, suggest a call within 48 hours of a reply, and stop after Bhai Dooj if there is none.

faqs.question: What do I say to a friend I have not spoken to in years at Diwali?
faqs.answer: Send one short message with a memory you share and one question that takes a sentence to answer, such as asking for one good thing from their year. Skip the long apology, because it puts the work of comforting you on them. If they reply, suggest a call with a day attached.

faqs.question: How long should a Diwali message on WhatsApp be?
faqs.answer: Under about 40 words for most people, and 20 to 30 for an old friend or a neighbour, so it fits one phone screen. 48.3% of the pages shared through SubhSandesh are opened on a phone. Close friends can get a longer message, up to about 60 words.

faqs.question: Do I need to reply to every Diwali wish in my society WhatsApp group?
faqs.answer: No. One short message from your household to the whole group is enough, and nobody expects 60 separate replies. Save individual messages for the neighbours who did you a specific favour this year.

faqs.question: What should I write to in-laws I am not very close to?
faqs.answer: Thank them for one concrete thing, such as a welcome, a recipe or help during the festival week, and use आप for elders. Keep it to two or three sentences and send it on the morning of Friday 29 October 2027, before the puja.

faqs.question: When should I send Diwali messages in 2027?
faqs.answer: Lakshmi Puja falls on Friday 29 October 2027. Send neighbours and the society group a message on the morning of Thursday 28 or Friday 29 October, in-laws on Friday morning, and close friends on Friday evening; Tamil Nadu families may mark Deepavali on Thursday 28 October.

faqs.question: Is it fine to send the same Diwali text to all my friends?
faqs.answer: It is fine for a group chat or the outer circle of acquaintances. For the five or so people closest to you, a copied text reads as a forward; add one memory or plan that only they would recognise.

faqs.question: Why don't cousins mind if I only message them at Diwali?
faqs.answer: Family ties hold up better through silence than friendships do. In Roberts and Dunbar's 18-month study, 70.3% of relatives in the inner network layer stayed there, against 48.6% of friends, so a once-a-year cousin message rarely feels cold.

faqs.question: What if my old friend does not reply to my Diwali message?
faqs.answer: Let it rest after Bhai Dooj on Sunday 31 October 2027 and try again on their birthday. A second nudge in the same week reads as pressure, and a late reply is still common in festival week.

faqs.question: Should I send Diwali messages to relatives in Hindi or English?
faqs.answer: Use the language you actually speak with that relative. If you write in Hindi, use Devanagari for elders who read it and add a Roman version for anyone who types in Hinglish.

faqs.question: Are these messages suitable for my parents or grandparents?
faqs.answer: Not really; this list is written for friends, cousins, in-laws and neighbours. Parents and grandparents usually value a call or a voice note on Diwali evening more than a typed line.

faqs.question: Can I turn one of these messages into an interactive Diwali card?
faqs.answer: Yes. SubhSandesh's Happy Diwali template has a friend mode and a family mode, and your lines can go on the row of wish diyas or in the letter inside the liffafa. It takes about five minutes and opens in any browser without an app or account.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Diwali Messages for Family and Friends, by How Close You Are

Diwali messages for family and friends land best when you sort them by closeness. A close friend gets a memory only the two of you share, a cousin gets family history, an in-law gets thanks, a neighbour gets gratitude for something specific, and an old friend gets one easy question. Keep each one short enough for a phone screen: 48.3% of the pages shared through SubhSandesh are opened on a phone, and a good one gets reread, at 11.1 views per page on average.

In our Raksha Bandhan 2026 data, the nearest festival we have measured (a small sample, n = 89), 49.4% of greeting pages were built on the festival day itself. For Diwali 2027 that day is Friday 29 October. Below are 21 original messages, a plan for restarting contact, and a table matching each relationship to length and send day.

## What separates a Diwali message from a forwarded greeting?

A Diwali message is written for one named person and mentions something only they would recognise. A forwarded greeting is the same text sent to everyone.

When Hill and Dunbar counted the people households sent Christmas cards to, the [average network reached 153.5 people, with 124.9 contacted directly](https://europepmc.org/article/MED/26189988), and relatives made up only about 21% of it (Human Nature, 2003; abstract read). A festival list is mostly friends, neighbours and the extended circle. Parents and grandparents usually need a call or a voice note more than a typed line, so they are left out here.

## Diwali messages for a close friend

Close friends sit in the innermost layer of what Robin Dunbar describes as a layered network. His 2016 paper in Royal Society Open Science describes [layers of roughly 5, 15, 50 and 150 people](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC4736918), each larger and less intimate. With the inner five, skip the formal blessing and write as you talk.

- "Twenty Diwalis of eating your mother's chakli and never once helping her fry it. This year I'm standing at the stove. Happy Diwali."
- "You know which of my stories are exaggerated and you laugh at them anyway. Happy Diwali to my favourite audience."
- "My diya count this year: one for the door, one for the mandir, one for you, for picking up every late-night call."
- "Same plan as always? Your terrace, my sweets, and both our mothers pretending not to notice we skipped the cleaning. Happy Diwali."
- "If this year were a rangoli, you'd be the outline that kept the colours from running. Shubh Deepavali, yaar."

## Diwali messages for an old friend you lost touch with

Losing touch is usually arithmetic, not a falling-out. In an 18-month study that combined phone records with surveys, Saramäki and colleagues found that [as new people entered a student's network, some old contacts were replaced or received fewer calls](https://europepmc.org/article/MED/24395777), because time for communication is finite (PNAS, 2014; abstract read). Diwali is a reason to reach back that needs no explanation.

- "Saw a box of kaju katli today and thought of the hostel room we shared. Happy Diwali. No need to catch me up on everything, just tell me one good thing from this year."
- "Three years of meaning to text you, and here I finally am. Happy Diwali. I'd like to hear your voice before the year runs out."
- "Your number was still saved under the nickname from school. Happy Diwali. I hope the lights are bright wherever you are now."
- "No group forward this time, just me: Happy Diwali. Free for a call on Sunday?"

Restarting contact takes three steps in Diwali week 2027. The third is knowing when to stop.

1. **Friday 29 October, evening:** one message, one shared memory, one question that takes a sentence to answer. Skip the long apology; it asks them to comfort you.
2. **Within 48 hours of a reply:** suggest a call with a day attached. Sunday 31 October, Bhai Dooj, falls on a weekend.
3. **No reply by Sunday night:** let it rest and try again on their birthday; a second nudge the same week reads as pressure.

## Diwali messages for cousins

Cousins forgive silence in a way friends do not. Roberts and Dunbar followed 25 English school leavers for 18 months and found that [70.3% of relatives in the inner network layer were still there at the end, against 48.6% of friends](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC4626528) (Human Nature, 2015). Friends who slipped to the outer layer lost closeness and relatives did not, so a cousin message can pick up as if you spoke last week.

- "Remember the year we ate the prasad ladoos before Nani had even lit the diya? Nani still brings it up. Happy Diwali, cousin."
- "These days we only meet at weddings. Let's add Diwali to that list. Happy Diwali, and hugs to the kids."
- "The cousins' group is 47 messages deep in Diwali GIFs, so here's one with actual words: miss you, proud of you, Happy Diwali."
- "Your side of the family always made the best chivda. Send me the recipe, or better, bring a jar next year. Happy Diwali."

## Diwali messages for in-laws

In-laws are kin by marriage, and the same Roberts and Dunbar paper notes that, in how contact relates to closeness, relatives by marriage follow the same rules as blood relatives. The difference is register. Use आप with elders and thank them for something concrete.

- "Thank you for the welcome you have given me in your home. Wishing you a peaceful, bright Diwali, Mummy ji and Papa ji."
- "Bhabhi, you taught me how this family sets the Lakshmi puja thali without once making me feel new. Happy Diwali."
- "To my brother-in-law, who carried every heavy box this week: Happy Diwali. The ladoos you hid are safe with me."
- इस घर की हर दिवाली में आपकी मेहनत की रोशनी है। शुभ दीपावली। — *Is ghar ki har Diwali mein aapki mehnat ki roshni hai. Shubh Deepavali.* — "Every Diwali in this home carries the light of your hard work. Happy Diwali."

## Diwali messages for neighbours and the society group

Neighbours sit near the outer 150 layer, so thanks for one specific favour beats a long blessing. For the society WhatsApp group, one short message from your household is enough, and nobody expects 60 separate replies.

- "From flat 302: thanks for the borrowed sugar, the parcels collected and the eye on our door while we were away. Happy Diwali."
- "Happy Diwali, aunty. Your diyas along the staircase are how our whole building knows it is festival week."
- "Happy Diwali from the Iyers in B-wing. Our door is open for sweets on Saturday evening, so do come by."
- "New to the building this year, and you already feel like neighbours. Happy Diwali. We'd love to drop off a box of sweets."

Send neighbour messages on the morning of Thursday 28 or Friday 29 October 2027, before the evening crowd of forwards. Tamil Nadu families may mark Deepavali on Thursday 28 October, per Drik Panchang's [Diwali 2027 calendar](https://www.drikpanchang.com/diwali/diwali-puja-calendar.html?year=2027), so a Thursday morning message covers both.

## Diwali messages by closeness, compared

The table matches each relationship to Dunbar's layer (our reading), a length, and a send day for 2027. The last column gives the SubhSandesh figure behind the advice.

| Who | Usual layer (Dunbar 2016) | Suggested length | When to send in 2027 | SubhSandesh figure |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Close friend | 5 | 30–60 words | Fri 29 Oct, evening | 11.1 views per page on average |
| Old friend, lost touch | 50–150 | 20–30 words plus one question | Fri 29 Oct; call by Sun 31 Oct | 48.3% of pages opened on a phone |
| Cousin | 15–50 | 25–40 words | Fri 29 Oct or Sun 31 Oct | 38.5% of creators add a password |
| In-laws | 15–50 | 25–40 words, आप register | Fri 29 Oct, before the puja | 49.4% of Raksha Bandhan pages built on the day (n = 89) |
| Neighbours | 150 | Under 30 words | Thu 28 or Fri 29 Oct, morning | 27.0% of Raksha Bandhan pages built the day before (n = 89) |

The closer the person, the longer the message can be. The Raksha Bandhan lines are a different festival and a small sample, so read them only as a rough guide to how late people leave things.

For the one or two people at the top of this table, a text can feel too small. SubhSandesh's [interactive Diwali card](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-diwali) has a friend mode and a family mode: they light a diya at their door with a tag from you, light a row of diyas that each lift one of your wishes, open your letter from a red-and-gold liffafa, and finish on a Shubh Deepavali card signed by you. It takes about five minutes and opens in any browser with no app or account.

For an old friend you have just reconnected with, [Capsule](https://subhsandesh.in/capsule) is not a Diwali template, but it gives you a reason to talk again: you both write predictions for the coming year, blind to each other, and it seals. A year later, around next Diwali, you open it together and score every one.

## When a typed Diwali message is the wrong choice

Dunbar's 2016 paper suggests that real relationships need at least occasional face-to-face contact to survive, and that friendships decay without it. If a friend lives ten minutes away, walking over with a box of sweets beats any message here. An elder who does not open links should get a phone call on Friday evening, after the puja.

A page is also the wrong tool for groups. The SubhSandesh card is one page for one person, not a broadcast, and it cannot post to a society group or a WhatsApp status. The template is new, so we have no Diwali usage data; every figure above is platform-wide or from Raksha Bandhan.

## Sources

- Hill, R. A. and Dunbar, R. I. M., [Social network size in humans](https://europepmc.org/article/MED/26189988), Human Nature, March 2003 (abstract read).
- Saramäki, J. et al., [Persistence of social signatures in human communication](https://europepmc.org/article/MED/24395777), PNAS, January 2014 (abstract read).
- Roberts, S. B. G. and Dunbar, R. I. M., [Managing relationship decay: network, gender, and contextual effects](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC4626528), Human Nature, October 2015 (full text).
- Dunbar, R. I. M., [Do online social media cut through the constraints that limit the size of offline social networks?](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC4736918), Royal Society Open Science, January 2016 (full text).
- Drik Panchang, [Diwali 2027 puja calendar](https://www.drikpanchang.com/diwali/diwali-puja-calendar.html?year=2027), date reference only.

sources.stat: Hill & Dunbar, Human Nature 2003 (abstract read): Christmas-card networks averaged a maximum of 153.5 individuals, 124.9 for those explicitly contacted; kin made up around 21%; contact frequency driven by distance and by emotional closeness and relatedness.

Saramäki et al., PNAS 2014 (abstract read): 18-month phone-record plus survey study of students leaving school; as new network members are added, some old members are replaced or receive fewer calls, attributed to finite resources such as time for communication.

Roberts & Dunbar, Human Nature 2015 (full text, CC BY): 25 English school leavers tracked 18 months; 102 of 145 kin (70.3%) in the inner layer at T1 remained there at T3 vs 69 of 142 friends (48.6%); moving to the outer layer cut emotional closeness for friends but not kin; affinal kin follow the same contact-closeness rules as genetic kin.

Dunbar, Royal Society Open Science 2016 (full text): network layers approximate 5, 15, 50 and 150; friendships have a natural decay rate in the absence of contact; real relationships may need occasional face-to-face interaction.
date/festival reference (not a cited competitor): Diwali 2027 calendar for New Delhi lists Lakshmi Puja Friday 29 October 2027, Narak Chaturdashi and Tamil Deepavali Thursday 28 October 2027.

serp.observations: Of the 10 seen on 2026-10-22: none had a comparison table, none cited research, none split messages for in-laws, neighbours or a lost-touch friend (jagranjosh has long-distance friends; greetingsisland mentions cousins and neighbours only in passing), and none gave 2027 send days.

Shared domains: bakingo, fnp, kamajewelry, adobe, pinterest (5); identical URLs at most 3 (bakingo, fnp, kamajewelry). Sub-intent kept distinct: messages by relationship closeness plus a restart-contact plan, not recipient-sorted quotes or classical lines.

structuralLimitations: Cannibalisation gate: 5 shared domains / up to 3 identical URLs with the anchor diwali-quotes SERP (BRIEF §9 threshold 4+ counted on URLs: at most 3; on domains: 5). Sub-intent sharpened to closeness tiers (lost-touch friend, cousins, in-laws, neighbours) and a dated restart plan; diwali-quotes' lost-touch FAQ and its Aknin & Sandstrom source were deliberately not reused.
No Diwali usage data exists; length and timing guidance uses platform-wide lines and the Raksha Bandhan 2026 analogue (n = 89), labelled in the body.
Hill & Dunbar 2003 and Saramäki et al. 2014 were read as abstracts only (not open access on Europe PMC full text); only abstract claims are used.
The 'affinal kin follow the same rules as genetic kin' point is Roberts & Dunbar 2015 citing Burton-Chellew & Dunbar 2011; the post attributes it to the 2015 paper's statement.
Mapping relationships to Dunbar's layers in the table is the post's own reading, marked '(our reading)' in the body.

Liu et al. 2023 (JPSP, reach-out appreciation) was relevant but already cited by diwali-wishes-maker for the lost-contact idea, so it was not reused. Firecrawl disconnected mid-run; SERP was measured before that with one Firecrawl search (India).

Parents and grandparents kept to a one-line pointer: sibling row diwali-wishes-for-family (row 49) owns them. In-laws are covered here because the row's angle names them; row 49 should avoid reusing these four lines.

failed.item: No source passes the **swap test** — none could sit unchanged in a different keyword's post in this batch
failed.why: Two of four papers are general network findings: Dunbar 2016 (layers of 5/15/50/150) and Saramäki et al. 2014 (old contacts get fewer calls as new ones join) could sit in a miss-you or lost-touch post largely unchanged. Hill & Dunbar 2003 (festival-card networks) and Roberts & Dunbar 2015 (kin vs friend decay, in-laws as kin) pass. Structural: no open-access study of festival or Diwali greeting exchange in India was found (Europe PMC/Crossref via findpapers.mjs: 'maintaining weak ties occasion messages', 'social network layers contact frequency emotional closeness', 'relationship decay friends contact', 'Christmas cards social network size'). Closes if a study of seasonal greeting exchange in an Indian sample is found outside the banned publishers.

auditReport.honestAssessment: An answer engine has a reason to cite this over the five ranking lists: it is the only page that ties who gets which message to measured network research (kin vs friend decay, festival-card network size) and gives a dated restart-contact plan for Diwali 2027, with length advice from SubhSandesh's own phone-open share. It cannot overcome the incumbents' domain authority, and two of its four papers are generic network findings; ranking, if it comes, takes months.
